keywords: Civil appeal – Preliminary objection to maintainability – Notice of appeal – Petition of appeal – Registered Attorney-at-Law – Absence of attorney\'s printed/name identification – Signature of registered attorney – Identity ascertainable from proxy and court record – No prejudice to respondent – Procedural irregularity – Substantial compliance – Liberal construction of procedural statutes – Substantive right of appeal – Procedural rules intended to advance justice – Technical defect not fatal – Access to appellate justice. The Court held that the omission of the registered attorney\'s name, where his identity and signature could otherwise be established, was not a fatal irregularity warranting dismissal of the appeal.
